title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed Bourbaki draft sheet, page '6-36' of redaction n° 392, slipped into the L-function notes. The neighbouring handwritten pages, on the functional equation of L-functions over function fields, have nothing to do with it; the sheet was presumably reused as scrap paper or simply misfiled.

The content is a set of exercises for Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative, ch. VII (Diviseurs), on determinantal (Fitting) ideals and invariant factors over Krull rings.

(g) Example over A = K[X,Y,Z], with m = (X,Y,Z) and q = (X, Y^2, YZ, Z^2). Take M = A/q and N = m/q. The claims are:
- d_0(M) = q and d_1(M) = A. These are immediate because M is cyclic.
- d_0(N) = m^2 and d_1(N) = m. To see this, present N on generators e1, e2, e3 (the images of X, Y, Z). The relations are e1 itself, together with X, Y, Z times e2 and X, Y, Z times e3. The 3×3 minors give m^2 and the 2×2 minors give m.
The example shows that the Fitting ideal of a submodule can be strictly smaller than that of the module (m^2 ⊊ q). Fitting ideals are therefore not monotone under passage to submodules, although they do grow under passage to quotients.

(11) Let A be a Krull ring and M, N finitely generated lattices in V, with dim V = n. Choose c ≠ 0 with cN ⊂ M and set d_k(N,M) = div(Fitt_k(M/cN)) − (n−k) div(c).
- (a) This is independent of c; it is called the determinantal divisor.
- (b) The d_k decrease in k, d_n = 0, and the invariant factors e_k = d_{n−k} − d_{n−k+1} increase in k. The proof is by reduction to the principal (DVR) case by localising at height-one primes.
- (c) d_0(N,M) equals the content χ(M,N) of the module M/N.
- (d) The definitions extend to a lattice N in a subspace W of lower dimension, by comparing with M ∩ W.

(12) Let A be noetherian and integrally closed, and N ⊂ M torsion-free of the same rank r.
- (a) ∧^k j is pseudo-injective, its cokernel is torsion, and χ(Coker ∧^k j) = C(r−1, k−1) χ(Coker j).
- (b) Consequently the torsion of ∧^k M is pseudo-null and c(∧^k M) = C(r−1, k−1) c(M). In particular c(det M) = c(M).
All of this is standard divisor-class theory for modules over Krull rings, as published in Bourbaki AC VII §4 (1965).
errors: No mathematical errors found. Example (g) checks out: the 3×3 minors of the relation matrix of N generate m^2, and its entries generate m.
In 11(c) the reference number '(n° )' is left blank in the typescript.
In 12(a), 'pour tout K' should read 'pour tout k'.
